_comment: THE VERSION SPINE (redesign plan 4D). One machine-readable record per outward-facing component: `current` is the latest PROVEN version (for a component layers/INDEX.json gateProven records, it is taken from gateProven and may never run ahead of it), `floors` is the minimum each CONSUMER needs, with the reason that consumer needs it, and `ids` is the package id, the aliases a host may install the SAME product under, and the `predecessors`: retired packages the product replaced (Dynamicweb.MCP before Truvio.Commerce.MCP). A predecessor is never an alias: a host that carries only a predecessor reads as BELOW the floor, never as matched and never as an absent optional app. Consumers legitimately differ: a floor belongs to the consumer that depends on it, never to the component. DERIVED COPIES: layers/base/base.contract.json `compat` copies the floors of the consumer `layers` (the spine is the source, the contract the copy) and tools/ci/Validate-Distribution.ps1 fails when they disagree. THE FLOOR RULE (owner ruling redesign-floors, 2026-09-23): a floor rises only when a consumer depends on the fix, never to the latest release. CI enforces it: a PR that raises any floor above the merge base must give the raised entry a NEW reason.ref naming the issue or PR the consumer depends on, and no floor may exceed `current`. VERSION ORDER: SemVer 2.0 with the NuGet reading of prerelease labels: a prerelease ranks below its release (0.6.0-beta < 0.6.0), labels compare case-insensitively (0.6.0-BETA == 0.6.0-beta), dot-separated identifiers compare numerically when both are numeric, a numeric identifier ranks below an alphanumeric one, and build metadata (+...) is ignored. A floor therefore names the version as the package ships it: a component released only as -beta states its floor as -beta. FLAGS: `flag` on a floor marks what the record could not settle: `untraced` (no issue or PR; the ref is the introducing commit), `no-reason-given` (the ref exists but states no dependency).

rule.text: A floor rises only when a consumer depends on the fix, never to the latest release.

reason.why: The layers ship DW 10.28.1 column names: feature-b2b-comms failed strict-mode deserialize on a 10.27.6 host while the static gate stayed green, which is the case the compat leg (#1061) was built for. The ring R1 is the outward claim the owner ruled on 2026-09-21 (Distribution #76); tfm net10.0 is the host runtime of that ring. Introduced in the contract by Distribution 60aac43b.

The package is packed at DynamicwebVersion 10.17.5 so the App Store dependency filter shows it to older hosts; 10.17.5 was compile-probed across 10.8 to 10.28 and the Alert/AlertType APIs are missing below it. The ring sentence was added by Serializer #22.
package.json compat.dw.min copies the base contract shape; the app reads /dwapi over HTTP and names no dependency of its own on 10.28.1.

DW_FLOOR 10.8.4: tested and packed at the floor, and verify-floor-binding.ps1 fails a DLL bound above it (releases 0.9.1 to 0.11.1 had shipped 10.28.1-bound). Compatible with 10.8 since the initial release (2f141da).
DW_FLOOR 10.27.13, the oldest host the app was verified on; a publish step checks the references stay at or below it.
DW_FLOOR 10.27.9 from the initial release: every 10.27 host qualifies. No verify-floor-binding step.
Rolling latest-only: the layers are authored for exactly one Swift release, so the floor is an equality pin that rolls forward with the release, never a range.
versions.json worksOn.swift ==2.4, the same rolling latest-only policy.
package.json compat.swift ==2.4: owner instruction 2026-09-12 to roll the Swift target to 2.4.

1.0.3-beta to 1.0.5-beta stopped remapping page ids held in option-list fields (ProductListComponentSelector, ProductComponentSelector, ProductBom), so a delivered surface-swift storefront listed zero products (gate run 20260922-231413). The chain below it: #30 (strict mode failed on declared heap keys before 1.0.5-beta), #21 (a Merge deleted every row of a keyless table before 1.0.3-beta), #18 (NULL round trip before 1.0.2-beta). Raised with sample-data 5.0.1, Distribution #78.
The serializer skills teach the 1.0-beta command names (Serialize, Deserialize, PackageDownload). Scoped to the skills that cover the Serializer.
0.6.0 adds skills inside MCP and Dynamo, which the estate builds on (owner ruling, Justin Sjouw, 2026-09-23). The owner expects this floor to rise again soon on the same basis.
